source: Image A is 60 mm wide and 40 mm high. Image C is 30 mm by 20

items.question: Image A is 60 mm wide and 40 mm high. Image C is 30 mm by 20 mm and image B is 40 mm by 20 mm. Which of B and C changed both sides by the same factor?
steps: A to C: 60 ÷ 2 = 30 and 40 ÷ 2 = 20, so both sides are multiplied by 1/2.
A to B: 60 − 20 = 40 and 40 − 20 = 20, so both sides lose the same 20 mm.
But for B the height factor is 20 ÷ 40 = 1/2, while the width factor is 40 ÷ 60 = 2/3.
The factors are different, so B is stretched; C used one factor, so it keeps the shape.
items.answer: C changed both sides by the factor 1/2, so it looks similar to A; B did not

videos.answer: C changed both sides by the factor 1/2, so it looks similar to A; B did not

source: Image A is 60 mm by 40 mm. Image D is 90 mm by 60 mm and ima

items.question: Image A is 60 mm by 40 mm. Image D is 90 mm by 60 mm and image E is 60 mm by 60 mm. Which of them changed proportionally?
steps: D: width factor 90 ÷ 60 = 3/2 and height factor 60 ÷ 40 = 3/2.
The two factors are the same, so D is A enlarged by 3/2.
E: width factor 60 ÷ 60 = 1 but height factor 60 ÷ 40 = 3/2.
The factors differ, so E is not proportional to A.
items.answer: D is proportional to A (factor 3/2 on both sides); E is not

videos.answer: D is proportional to A (factor 3/2 on both sides); E is not

source: Figure it Out (ratios and proportions, question 4)

items.question: Look at the five rectangles A, B, C, D and E. Which rectangles are similar to each other? You can verify this by measuring the width and height using a scale and comparing their ratios.
steps: Measure the width and the height of each rectangle with a scale.
Write width : height for each rectangle.
Reduce each ratio to its simplest form by dividing both terms by their HCF.
Rectangles whose simplest forms are the same are similar; the others are not.
items.answer: Rectangles with the same width to height ratio in simplest form are similar

videos.answer: Rectangles with the same width to height ratio in simplest form are similar

source: Figure it Out (ratios and proportions, question 5)

items.question: Look at the given rectangle. Can you draw a smaller rectangle and a bigger rectangle with the same width to height ratio in your notebooks? Compare your rectangles with your classmates' drawings. Are all of them the same? If they are different from yours, can you think why? Are they wrong?
steps: Measure the rectangle and write width : height, for example 6 cm : 4 cm, which is 3 : 2.
For a smaller one, multiply both sides by one factor less than 1: 6 × 1/2 = 3 and 4 × 1/2 = 2.
For a bigger one, multiply both sides by one factor more than 1: 6 × 2 = 12 and 4 × 2 = 8.
Classmates may use other factors, so the sizes differ, but every drawing with ratio 3 : 2 is correct.
items.answer: Yes; drawings of different sizes are all correct as long as their width to height ratio is the same

videos.answer: Yes; drawings of different sizes are all correct as long as their width to height ratio is the same

source: Figure it Out (ratios and proportions, question 7)

items.question: Let us draw some human figures. Measure your friend's body: the lengths of their head, torso, arms and legs. Write the ratios head : torso, torso : arms and torso : legs. Now draw a figure with head, torso, arms and legs in equivalent ratios. Does the drawing look more realistic if the ratios are proportional? Why? Why not?
steps: Measure the four lengths, for example head 20 cm, torso 60 cm, arms 60 cm, legs 80 cm.
Write the ratios: head : torso is 20 : 60, which is 1 : 3; torso : legs is 60 : 80, which is 3 : 4.
Choose one factor for the drawing, for example 1/10: 20 × 1/10 = 2 cm for the head and 60 × 1/10 = 6 cm for the torso.
Scaling every length by the same factor keeps the ratios, so the figure looks realistic.
items.answer: Yes; when every length is scaled by the same factor, the ratios stay the same and the figure looks realistic

videos.answer: Yes; when every length is scaled by the same factor, the ratios stay the same and the figure looks realistic

source: Write the width to height ratio of image A (60 mm by 40 mm)

items.question: Write the width to height ratio of image A (60 mm by 40 mm) and say what it means. Then multiply both terms by 1/2 and say which image you get.
steps: Width to height of image A is 60 : 40, with terms 60 and 40.
It means for every 60 mm of width there are 40 mm of height.
Multiply both terms by 1/2: 60 × 1/2 = 30 and 40 × 1/2 = 20.
The new ratio is 30 : 20, which is image C.
items.answer: 60 : 40, for every 60 mm of width there are 40 mm of height; halving both terms gives 30 : 20, image C

videos.answer: 60 : 40, for every 60 mm of width there are 40 mm of height; halving both terms gives 30 : 20, image C

source: Reduce the width to height ratios of images A (60 : 40), D (

items.question: Reduce the width to height ratios of images A (60 : 40), D (90 : 60), B (40 : 20) and E (60 : 60) to simplest form. Which are in proportion with A?
steps: A: the HCF of 60 and 40 is 20; 60 ÷ 20 = 3 and 40 ÷ 20 = 2, so 3 : 2.
D: the HCF of 90 and 60 is 30; 90 ÷ 30 = 3 and 60 ÷ 30 = 2, so 3 : 2.
E: the HCF is 60; 60 ÷ 60 = 1, so 1 : 1.
Only D matches 3 : 2, so 60 : 40 :: 90 : 60. The factor from A to D is 90 ÷ 60 = 3/2.
items.answer: A and D are both 3 : 2, so 60 : 40 :: 90 : 60; B (2 : 1) and E (1 : 1) are not in proportion with A

videos.answer: A and D are both 3 : 2, so 60 : 40 :: 90 : 60; B (2 : 1) and E (1 : 1) are not in proportion with A

source: Are the ratios 3 : 4 and 72 : 96 proportional?

items.question: Are the ratios 3 : 4 and 72 : 96 proportional?
steps: 3 : 4 is already in simplest form, because the HCF of 3 and 4 is 1.
The HCF of 72 and 96 is 24.
The simplest forms are the same, so 3 : 4 :: 72 : 96.
items.answer: Yes, 72 : 96 reduces to 3 : 4, so the ratios are proportional

videos.answer: Yes, 72 : 96 reduces to 3 : 4, so the ratios are proportional

source: Regular filter coffee is 15 mL decoction to 35 mL milk, stro

items.question: Regular filter coffee is 15 mL decoction to 35 mL milk, strong is 20 : 30 and light is 10 : 40. Explain why the strong one is stronger and the light one is lighter.
steps: Simplest forms: 15 : 35 is 3 : 7, 20 : 30 is 2 : 3, 10 : 40 is 1 : 4.
Decoction for each mL of milk, regular: 15 ÷ 35 = 3/7 ≈ 0.43.
Strong: 20 ÷ 30 ≈ 0.67, which is more than 0.43, so more decoction for the same milk.
Light: 10 ÷ 40 = 0.25, which is less than 0.43, so less decoction for the same milk.
items.answer: Strong coffee has more decoction for each mL of milk (2 : 3 against 3 : 7); light coffee has less (1 : 4)

videos.answer: Strong coffee has more decoction for each mL of milk (2 : 3 against 3 : 7); light coffee has less (1 : 4)

source: Try This (filter coffee table)

items.question: Manjunath mixes coffee decoction with milk in these amounts: 300 mL with 600 mL, 150 mL with 500 mL, 200 mL with 400 mL, 24 mL with 56 mL, and 100 mL with 300 mL. Regular coffee is 15 mL decoction with 35 mL milk. Is each one regular, strong or light?
steps: Regular is 15 : 35, which is 3 : 7, and 15 ÷ 35 = 3/7 ≈ 0.43.
300 : 600 is 1 : 2 and 300 ÷ 600 = 0.5, more than 0.43, so strong.
150 : 500 is 3 : 10 and 150 ÷ 500 = 0.3, less than 0.43, so light.
200 : 400 is 1 : 2, so strong.
24 : 56 is 3 : 7, the same as regular, so regular.
100 : 300 is 1 : 3 and 100 ÷ 300 ≈ 0.33, less than 0.43, so light.
items.answer: 300 : 600 strong, 150 : 500 light, 200 : 400 strong, 24 : 56 regular, 100 : 300 light

videos.answer: 300 : 600 strong, 150 : 500 light, 200 : 400 strong, 24 : 56 regular, 100 : 300 light

source: Figure it Out (ratios and proportions, question 1)

items.question: Circle the following statements of proportion that are true. (i) 4 : 7 :: 12 : 21 (ii) 8 : 3 :: 24 : 6 (iii) 7 : 12 :: 12 : 7 (iv) 21 : 6 :: 35 : 10 (v) 12 : 18 :: 28 : 12 (vi) 24 : 8 :: 9 : 3
steps: Reduce each ratio to its simplest form and compare.
(i) 12 : 21 is 4 : 7, the same as 4 : 7, so true.
(ii) 24 : 6 is 4 : 1, but 8 : 3 is already in simplest form, so false.
(iii) 7 : 12 and 12 : 7 have their terms in a different order, so false.
(iv) 21 : 6 is 7 : 2 and 35 : 10 is 7 : 2, so true.
(v) 12 : 18 is 2 : 3 and 28 : 12 is 7 : 3, so false.
(vi) 24 : 8 is 3 : 1 and 9 : 3 is 3 : 1, so true.
items.answer: (i), (iv) and (vi) are true

videos.answer: (i), (iv) and (vi) are true

source: Figure it Out (ratios and proportions, question 6)

items.question: A long brick wall has patterns made using grey and coloured bricks, and each wall continues its pattern throughout. In wall (a), one block of the pattern has 2, 3 and 4 grey bricks in its rows and 3, 2 and 1 coloured bricks. In wall (b), one block has 16 grey bricks and 12 coloured bricks. What is the ratio of grey bricks to coloured bricks? Give the ratios in simplest form.
steps: Wall (a): grey bricks in one block are 2 + 3 + 4 = 9.
Coloured bricks in one block are 3 + 2 + 1 = 6.
9 : 6 has HCF 3, so the simplest form is 3 : 2.
Wall (b): 16 : 12 has HCF 4, so the simplest form is 4 : 3.
The pattern repeats, so the whole wall has the same ratio as one block.
items.answer: (a) 9 : 6, which is 3 : 2; (b) 16 : 12, which is 4 : 3

videos.answer: (a) 9 : 6, which is 3 : 2; (b) 16 : 12, which is 4 : 3

steps: Orange juice to apple juice is 600 : 900.

items.question: Kesang uses 10 spoons of sugar for 6 glasses of lemonade. How many spoons does she need for 18 glasses in all with the same sweetness?
steps: Glasses to spoons: 6 : 10 :: 18 : ?
Factor of change for the glasses: 18 ÷ 6 = 3.
Spoons change by the same factor: 10 × 3 = 30.
items.answer: 30 spoons of sugar

videos.answer: 30 spoons of sugar

items.question: Nitin builds a 60 ft wall with 3 bags of cement and Hari builds a 40 ft wall with 2 bags. Are the walls equally strong?

items.answer: Yes, both walls use one bag for every 20 ft, so they are equally strong

source: Figure it Out (ratios and proportions, question 3)

items.question: Fill in the missing numbers for these ratios that are proportional to 18 : 24. 3 : ___, 12 : ___, 20 : ___, 27 : ___
steps: Simplest form first: the HCF of 18 and 24 is 6, so 18 : 24 is 3 : 4.

source: Example (teachers and students in your school)

items.question: In my school, there are 5 teachers and 170 students. The ratio of teachers to students in my school is 5 : 170. Count the number of teachers and students in your school. What is the ratio of teachers to students in your school? Is it proportional to the one in my school?
steps: Simplest form of 5 : 170: the HCF is 5, so it is 1 : 34.
Count your school, for example 12 teachers and 360 students: 12 : 360.
The HCF of 12 and 360 is 12, so 12 : 360 is 1 : 30.
1 : 30 is not 1 : 34, so the two ratios are not proportional; your school has fewer students for each teacher.
items.answer: 5 : 170 is 1 : 34; your school's ratio is proportional only if it also reduces to 1 : 34

videos.answer: 5 : 170 is 1 : 34; your school's ratio is proportional only if it also reduces to 1 : 34

source: Example (blackboard rectangle)

items.question: Measure the width and height (to the nearest cm) of the blackboard in your classroom. What is the ratio of width to height of the blackboard? Can you draw a rectangle in your notebook whose width and height are proportional to the ratio of the blackboard? Compare the rectangle you have drawn to those drawn by your classmates. Do they all look the same?
steps: Measure, for example, width 360 cm and height 120 cm: 360 : 120.
The HCF is 120, so the simplest form is 3 : 1.
Draw a rectangle 3 cm wide and 1 cm high, or 9 cm by 3 cm: any pair in the ratio 3 : 1.
Classmates' rectangles may be different sizes, but all with ratio 3 : 1 have the same shape.
items.answer: The blackboard's ratio in simplest form, for example 3 : 1; every rectangle in that ratio has the same shape though sizes differ

videos.answer: The blackboard's ratio in simplest form, for example 3 : 1; every rectangle in that ratio has the same shape though sizes differ

source: A cook makes 15 kg of rice for 120 students. On a rainy day

items.question: A cook makes 15 kg of rice for 120 students. On a rainy day only 80 students come. How much rice should the cook make?
steps: Students to rice: 120 : 15 :: 80 : ?
Factor of change: 80 ÷ 120 = 2/3.
items.answer: 10 kg of rice

videos.answer: 10 kg of rice

source: Check by cross multiplication that 120 : 15 :: 80 : 10, then

items.question: Check by cross multiplication that 120 : 15 :: 80 : 10, then use Aryabhata's rule to find the fourth term of 120 : 15 :: 80 : ?
steps: Outer terms: 120 × 10 = 1200.
Inner terms: 15 × 80 = 1200, so ad = bc and the ratios are proportional.
Pramana 120, phala 15, ichchha 80.
Phala times ichchha: 15 × 80 = 1200; divide by the pramana: 1200 ÷ 120 = 10.
items.answer: ad = bc holds (1200 = 1200); the fourth term is 10

videos.answer: ad = bc holds (1200 = 1200); the fourth term is 10

source: A car travels 90 km in 150 minutes. At the same speed, how f

items.question: A car travels 90 km in 150 minutes. At the same speed, how far does it go in 4 hours?
steps: 4 hours is 4 × 60 = 240 minutes, so the proportion is 150 : 90 :: 240 : x.
Cross multiply: 150 × x = 240 × 90.
items.answer: 144 km

videos.answer: 144 km

items.question: The Earth travels approximately 940 million kilometres around the Sun in a year. How many kilometres will it travel in a week?
steps: A year has about 52 weeks.
Distance to weeks: 940000000 : 52 :: x : 1.
items.answer: About 18076923 km in a week

videos.answer: About 18076923 km in a week

source: Figure it Out (rule of three, question 2)

items.question: A mason is building a house in the shape shown in the diagram, with walls of 12 ft, 15 ft, 9 ft, 9 ft and 6 ft and an inner wall that separates two rooms. To build a wall of 10 feet, he requires approximately 1450 bricks. How many bricks would he need to build the house? Assume all walls are of the same height and thickness.
steps: Add all the outer walls and the inner wall: 12 + 12 + 12 + 15 + 9 + 15 + 9 + 9 + 9 + 6 = 108 ft.
Wall length to bricks: 10 : 1450 :: 108 : x.
items.answer: About 15660 bricks

videos.answer: About 15660 bricks

source: Activity (cook a dish for 15 guests)

items.question: Take your favourite dish. Find out all the ingredients and their respective quantities needed to make the dish for your family. Suppose you are celebrating a festival and you want to invite 15 guests. Find out the quantities of the ingredients required to cook the same dish for them.
steps: List each ingredient for your family, for example 5 people: 2 cups of rice, 1 cup of dal.
Factor of change from 5 people to 15 guests: 15 ÷ 5 = 3.
Multiply every ingredient by the same factor: 2 × 3 = 6 cups of rice and 1 × 3 = 3 cups of dal.
Every ingredient must use the same factor, or the dish will taste different.
items.answer: Multiply every ingredient by the same factor, guests ÷ family size

videos.answer: Multiply every ingredient by the same factor, guests ÷ family size

source: Figure it Out (unit conversions, question 2)

items.question: Last year, we hired 3 buses for the school trip. We had a total of 162 students and teachers who went on that trip and all the buses were full. This year we have 204 students. How many buses will we need? Will all the buses be full?
steps: Each bus holds 162 ÷ 3 = 54 people.
Buses needed: 204 ÷ 54 ≈ 3.78, so 3 buses are not enough and we need 4.
4 buses hold 4 × 54 = 216 people.
216 − 204 = 12 seats stay empty, so not all buses are full.
items.answer: 4 buses; they will not all be full (12 seats empty)

videos.answer: 4 buses; they will not all be full (12 seats empty)

source: Figure it Out (unit conversions, question 5)

items.question: Let us try an ancient problem from Lilavati. At that time weights were measured in a unit named palas and niskas was a unit of money. "If 2.5 palas of saffron costs 3/7 niskas, O expert businessman! tell me quickly what quantity of saffron can be bought for 9 niskas?"
steps: Niskas to palas: 3/7 : 2.5 :: 9 : x.
Cross multiply: 3/7 × x = 2.5 × 9.
items.answer: 52.5 palas of saffron

videos.answer: 52.5 palas of saffron

source: Figure it Out (unit conversions, question 7)

items.question: The mass of equal volumes of gold and water are in the ratio 37 : 2. If 1 litre of water is 1 kg in mass, what is the mass of 1 litre of gold?
steps: Gold to water is 37 : 2 :: x : 1.
Cross multiply: 2 × x = 37 × 1.

source: Figure it Out (unit conversions, question 9)

items.question: A tap takes 15 seconds to fill a mug of water. The volume of the mug is 500 mL. How much time does the same tap take to fill a bucket of water if the bucket has a 10 litre capacity?
steps: Same units: 10 litres is 10000 mL.
Factor of change: 10000 ÷ 500 = 20.
Time: 20 × 15 = 300 seconds.
300 ÷ 60 = 5 minutes.
items.answer: 300 seconds, which is 5 minutes

videos.answer: 300 seconds, which is 5 minutes

source: Neelima is 3 and her mother is 10 times as old. What is the

items.question: Neelima is 3 and her mother is 10 times as old. What is the ratio of their ages now, and when Neelima is 12?
steps: Mother's age now: 3 × 10 = 30, so the ratio is 3 : 30, which is 1 : 10.
Neelima is 12 after 12 − 3 = 9 years; her mother is then 30 + 9 = 39.
The ratio becomes 12 : 39; the HCF is 3, so it is 4 : 13.
1 : 10 and 4 : 13 are different, so the ratio did not stay the same.
items.answer: 1 : 10 now and 4 : 13 when Neelima is 12; the ratio changes

videos.answer: 1 : 10 now and 4 : 13 when Neelima is 12; the ratio changes

source: Puneeth's father rides from Lucknow to Kanpur in 2 hours at

items.question: Puneeth's father rides from Lucknow to Kanpur in 2 hours at 50 km/h. How long does the trip take at 75 km/h?
steps: The Rule of Three would give 2 × 75 ÷ 50 = 3 hours, more time at a higher speed, so it is wrong.
The distance stays the same: 50 × 2 = 100 km.
Time at 75 km/h: 100 ÷ 75 = 4/3 hours.
4/3 hours is 1 hour and 20 minutes, less than 2 hours.
items.answer: 1 hour 20 minutes; speed and time are not proportional, so the Rule of Three does not apply

videos.answer: 1 hour 20 minutes; speed and time are not proportional, so the Rule of Three does not apply

source: Figure it Out (unit conversions, question 6)

items.question: Harmain is a 1 year old girl. Her elder brother is 5 years old. What will be Harmain's age when the ratio of her age to her brother's age is 1 : 2?
steps: The brother is always 5 − 1 = 4 years older, an additive change.
Let Harmain be x years old; her brother is x + 4 and we need x : (x + 4) = 1 : 2.
Cross multiply: 2x = x + 4, so x = 4.
Check: 4 : 8 is 1 : 2.
items.answer: Harmain will be 4 years old

videos.answer: Harmain will be 4 years old

source: Figure it Out (unit conversions, question 11)

items.question: A tractor can plough the same area of a field 4 times faster than a pair of oxen. A farmer wants to plough his 20 acre field. A pair of oxen takes 6 hours to plough an acre of land. How much time would it take if the farmer used a pair of oxen to plough the field? How much time would it take him if he decides to use a tractor instead?
steps: Oxen: area and time are proportional, so 20 × 6 = 120 hours.
A tractor 4 times faster takes less time, not more: 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5 hours for one acre.
Tractor for the field: 20 × 1.5 = 30 hours.
items.answer: 120 hours with oxen and 30 hours with a tractor

videos.answer: 120 hours with oxen and 30 hours with a tractor

source: Himachal tea costs ₹200 for 200 g. Meghalaya tea costs ₹800

items.question: Himachal tea costs ₹200 for 200 g. Meghalaya tea costs ₹800 for 1 kg. Which tea is more expensive?
steps: Same unit: 1 kg is 1000 g, so the ratios are 200 : 200 and 1000 : 800.
Simplest forms: 1 : 1 and 5 : 4, so they are not proportional.
200 g is 1/5 of 1 kg, so 1 kg of Himachal tea costs 200 × 5 = 1000 rupees.
1 kg of Meghalaya tea costs 800 rupees, and 1000 is more than 800.
items.answer: Himachal tea is more expensive: ₹1000 a kg against ₹800 a kg

videos.answer: Himachal tea is more expensive: ₹1000 a kg against ₹800 a kg

source: A sachet of 6 mL costs ₹2, a 180 mL bottle ₹154, a 340 mL bo

items.question: A sachet of 6 mL costs ₹2, a 180 mL bottle ₹154, a 340 mL bottle ₹276 and a 1000 mL bottle ₹540. Which size gives the cheapest shampoo per mL?
steps: Sachet: 2 ÷ 6 ≈ 0.33 rupees per mL.
Small bottle: 154 ÷ 180 ≈ 0.86 rupees per mL; medium: 276 ÷ 340 ≈ 0.81.
Large bottle: 540 ÷ 1000 = 0.54 rupees per mL.
Volumes 6 : 180 is 1 : 30 but prices 2 : 154 is 1 : 77, so they are not proportional.
items.answer: The sachet is cheapest per mL here (about ₹0.33), then the large bottle (₹0.54); price is not proportional to volume

videos.answer: The sachet is cheapest per mL here (about ₹0.33), then the large bottle (₹0.54); price is not proportional to volume

source: Figure it Out (unit conversions, question 3)

items.question: The area of Delhi is 1484 sq. km and the area of Mumbai is 550 sq. km. The population of Delhi is approximately 30 million and that of Mumbai is 20 million people. Which city is more crowded? Why do you say so?
steps: Compare people for each sq. km, not the totals.
Delhi: 30000000 ÷ 1484 ≈ 20216 people per sq. km.
Mumbai: 20000000 ÷ 550 ≈ 36364 people per sq. km.
36364 is more than 20216, so Mumbai has more people in each sq. km.
items.answer: Mumbai is more crowded: about 36364 people per sq. km against about 20216 in Delhi

videos.answer: Mumbai is more crowded: about 36364 people per sq. km against about 20216 in Delhi

source: Share 12 counters in the ratio 3 : 1, and then 42 counters i

items.question: Share 12 counters in the ratio 3 : 1, and then 42 counters in the ratio 4 : 3.
steps: 12 in 3 : 1: one round takes 3 + 1 = 4 counters, and 12 ÷ 4 = 3 rounds.
Partner: 3 × 3 = 9; you: 1 × 3 = 3.
42 in 4 : 3: there are 4 + 3 = 7 groups, each of 42 ÷ 7 = 6.
items.answer: 12 shared 3 : 1 gives 9 and 3; 42 shared 4 : 3 gives 24 and 18

videos.answer: 12 shared 3 : 1 gives 9 and 3; 42 shared 4 : 3 gives 24 and 18

source: Prashanti invests ₹75000 and Bhuvan ₹25000. They share a pro

items.question: Prashanti invests ₹75000 and Bhuvan ₹25000. They share a profit of ₹4000 in the ratio of their investments. What does each get?
steps: Ratio of investments: 75000 : 25000; the HCF is 25000, so it is 3 : 1.
Number of groups: 3 + 1 = 4; each group is 4000 ÷ 4 = 1000.
items.answer: Prashanti gets ₹3000 and Bhuvan gets ₹1000

videos.answer: Prashanti gets ₹3000 and Bhuvan gets ₹1000

source: A 40 kg mixture has sand and cement in the ratio 3 : 1. How

items.question: A 40 kg mixture has sand and cement in the ratio 3 : 1. How much cement must be added to make the ratio 5 : 2?
steps: Groups: 3 + 1 = 4, each 40 ÷ 4 = 10 kg; sand is 3 × 10 = 30 kg and cement 10 kg.
Sand stays 30 kg, so 5 : 2 :: 30 : ?
The second term is 2/5 of the first: 2/5 × 30 = 12 kg of cement.
Cement to add: 12 − 10 = 2 kg.
items.answer: 2 kg of cement

videos.answer: 2 kg of cement

source: Figure it Out (ratio sharing, question 1)

items.question: Divide ₹4500 into two parts in the ratio 2 : 3.
steps: Groups: 2 + 3 = 5.
One group: 4500 ÷ 5 = 900.

source: Figure it Out (ratio sharing, question 2)

items.question: In a science lab, acid and water are mixed in the ratio of 1 : 5 to make a solution. In a bottle that has 240 mL of the solution, how much acid and water does the solution contain?
steps: Groups: 1 + 5 = 6.
One group: 240 ÷ 6 = 40 mL.
Acid: 1 × 40 = 40 mL; water: 5 × 40 = 200 mL.
items.answer: 40 mL of acid and 200 mL of water

videos.answer: 40 mL of acid and 200 mL of water

source: Figure it Out (ratio sharing, question 3)

items.question: Blue and yellow paints are mixed in the ratio of 3 : 5 to produce green paint. To produce 40 mL of green paint, how much of these two colours are needed? To make the paint a lighter shade of green, I added 20 mL of yellow to the mixture. What is the new ratio of blue and yellow in the paint?
steps: Groups: 3 + 5 = 8; one group: 40 ÷ 8 = 5 mL.
Blue: 3 × 5 = 15 mL; yellow: 5 × 5 = 25 mL.
After adding yellow: 25 + 20 = 45 mL of yellow.
New ratio 15 : 45; the HCF is 15, so it is 1 : 3.
items.answer: 15 mL of blue and 25 mL of yellow; the new ratio is 1 : 3

videos.answer: 15 mL of blue and 25 mL of yellow; the new ratio is 1 : 3

source: Figure it Out (ratio sharing, question 4)

items.question: To make soft idlis, you need to mix rice and urad dal in the ratio of 2 : 1. If you need 6 cups of this mixture to make idlis tomorrow morning, how many cups of rice and urad dal will you need?
steps: Groups: 2 + 1 = 3.
One group: 6 ÷ 3 = 2 cups.
Rice: 2 × 2 = 4 cups; urad dal: 1 × 2 = 2 cups.
items.answer: 4 cups of rice and 2 cups of urad dal

videos.answer: 4 cups of rice and 2 cups of urad dal

source: Figure it Out (ratio sharing, question 5)

items.question: I have one bucket of orange paint that I made by mixing red and yellow paints in the ratio of 3 : 5. I added another bucket of yellow paint to this mixture. What is the ratio of red paint to yellow paint in the new mixture?
steps: Take both buckets to hold the same amount, and split one bucket into 3 + 5 = 8 equal groups.
The orange bucket has 3 groups of red and 5 groups of yellow.
A full bucket of yellow adds 8 more groups of yellow: 5 + 8 = 13.
Red to yellow is now 3 : 13.

items.question: A crane of height 155 cm has its neck and the rest of its body in the ratio 4 : 6. For your height, if your neck and the rest of the body also had this ratio, how tall would your neck be?
steps: Groups: 4 + 6 = 10; the neck takes 4 of every 10 parts of the height.
For the crane: 4 ÷ 10 × 155 = 62 cm of neck.
For your height, say 150 cm: 4 ÷ 10 × 150 = 60 cm.
So your neck would be 4/10 of your height.
items.answer: 4/10 of your height, for example 60 cm for a height of 150 cm (the crane's neck is 62 cm)

items.question: In a Binairo row of 6 cells, the first two cells hold horizontal lines and the fifth holds a vertical line. Fill the row.
steps: Two horizontal lines are adjacent, so the third cell must be a vertical line.
A row of 6 cells needs 3 of each symbol; so far there are 2 horizontal and 2 vertical.
The fourth cell next to a vertical pair would make three verticals if cells 3, 4 and 5 were all vertical, so cell 4 is horizontal.
That makes 3 horizontal lines, so cell 6 is vertical: H H V H V V.
items.answer: H H V H V V
